_meta.warning: This file captures the LITERAL regexes and marker lists verbatim. It does NOT capture the control flow — ExtractCannabinoids() is genuinely procedural (ordered branches, ratio orientation, per-serving-to-pack reconciliation, name-first identity resolution), not a flat priority-match loop. Port the algorithm as Go code in internal/resolve/cannabinoids.go, using these patterns as the named, loaded-from-JSON source of truth for each regex — do not re-derive the regexes from memory, and do not flatten the control flow into a data-driven list it was never shaped as. See harvest/NOTES.md for the full explanation.
_meta.canonical_test_product: Cannavedic - CannEx Strong Plus THC+CBD Extract (10:1 THC:CBD) 1000mg | 1ml -> thc_mg=909, cbd_mg=91, THC-dominant

notes.cbd_label_first_vs_num_first: Label-first ("CBD 91mg") is preferred over number-first ("91mg CBD") — in lists like "THC 909mg CBD 91mg" each number belongs to the cannabinoid it FOLLOWS. Number-first tolerates "of/the/pure" ("500mg of CBD"). All matches are scanned and the MAX taken: per-serving figures ("2.1mg of CBD per drop") are always smaller than the pack-level figure in the same text.
notes.nul_before_zero_in_thc_free: The \b before 0 in thc_free is load-bearing: without it, "5(0% THC)" inside "50% THC" matched, marking half the balanced catalogue THC-free. Never simplify this regex.
notes.trace_thc_is_not_dosed: trace_thc ("<0.3% THC", "non-psychoactive") means THC is a legal-compliance disclaimer, not a dosed cannabinoid — a "CBD Oil 2000mg ... contains <0.3% THC" is 2000mg of CBD, not 2000mg of mystery total.
notes.cannabinoid_pair_scrub: A number adjacent to "CBD + THC" / "THC/CBD" (the pair, not a ratio) is combined content — scrub the pair text before per-cannabinoid extraction so it can't be misattributed to one side. ':' is deliberately excluded from the separator class — "THC:CBD 10:1" is a ratio, not a pair mention.
notes.percentages_are_full_decimals: 0.3% THC is a valid small value, not zero — this was a shipped bug (see thc_free note).
notes.gram_isolates: Isolates are sold by grams ("100% CBD - 5gm" = 5000mg) — pct_cbd/pct_thc compute against a volume_ml base first, falling back to weight_g (1g ~= 1000mg) when no ml volume exists.
notes.per_serving_reconciliation: Explicit per-cannabinoid figures far below the pack-level name total ((cbd+thc)*5 <= total) are scaled up preserving their ratio — "1000mg pack, 2.1+2.1mg per drop" becomes 500/500, not 2.1/2.1.
notes.name_first_identity: The headline total mg is resolved NAME-FIRST — descriptions carry raw-herb weights ("10000mg of Strong Vijaya Extract") and pack-variant figures that are NOT this product's cannabinoid content.
notes.equal_bare_ratio_needs_no_orientation: A bare ratio ("1:1", "(10:1)") that is EQUAL splits 50/50 whenever both cannabinoids are textually in play, with no dominant-cannabinoid determination needed. An UNEQUAL bare ratio needs a determinable dominant (from thc_dominant_wording or name-first identity) before it can be oriented.
notes.unoriented_ratio_stays_honest_total: An unequal bare ratio with no determinable dominant ("THC+CBD (2:1)", direction unstated) must NOT be guessed at — it stays concentration_type=total rather than assuming an orientation that could contradict the label.
notes.balanced_pair_no_split_assumption: An explicit "CBD + THC" pair with NO printed ratio and no determinable dominant is assumed market-standard balanced 1:1 — the neutral/maximum-entropy estimate for Indian full-spectrum products sold without a printed split. This gives both cbd_price_per_mg and thc_price_per_mg with bounded error instead of an unusable total-only bucket. Guarded: skipped if an unoriented bare ratio is present (would contradict a printed but undirected split).
notes.dominant_basis_finalize_threshold: In finalize(), a cannabinoid >= 3x the other makes the product cbd- or thc-dominant (concentration_type = that basis, but BOTH cbd_mg and thc_mg are still captured, never zeroed). Below 3x, concentration_type = total.

hemp_seed_gate: A product is hemp_seed (cannabinoids all zero, PriceInr/mg = NULL forever) when hemp_seed pattern matches AND the text does not also mention 'cbd' or 'vijaya'. This is checked NAME-FIRST (a product literally named "Hemp Seed Oil" is seed oil full stop, even if the description name-drops CBD for comparison) and again as a description-level fallback.
